name: flour_prices
title: Tiao and Box's tools: flour prices in three cities
summary: The Wisconsin tools on the data Tiao and Tsay (1989) analysed: monthly flour price indices in Buffalo, Minneapolis and Kansas City, 1972-1980, from three univariate models built with art's identification. Box and Tiao's (1977) canonical analysis of the levels and Tiao and Box's (1981) stepwise M(l) say what the univariates' differences hide: the prices move together, and the joint model may not need every difference. Then the cointegration question (N1c): the rank by parametric bootstrap (drvec, B = 499, shipped in the example's cache) does NOT reject r = 0, and the example goes one rank further on theory, written as such, to show the VEC's nodes.
plan: N1 run_gate — the three univariate models, certified
N1b canonical_analysis — Box and Tiao (1977) on the levels: one common trend, and a contrast between markets
N2 identify_cross — innovations correlated at 0.96: the same shocks
N2 identify_matrices — Tiao and Box's stepwise M(l) beside Jenkins and Alavi's S_k, on the differences
N3 estimate — the VAR(1) M(l) asks for
N5 evaluate — the yardstick: does it forecast better than the univariates?
N1c prepare_vec — the cointegration question; purpose "long run"; p = 2 from M(l) on the levels, case pre
C1 rank_test (B = 499, cached) — r = 0 is not rejected (LR 14.35 against 20.06, p 0.19): the differences hold
C2 estimate_vec r = 1 ON THEORY — the contrast between markets, beside the canonical weights
C3 test_restriction — who corrects, by LR
C5 long_run, C6 the level responses with the bootstrap's bands (irf_bands, cached)
C8 evaluate — the yardstick for the VEC: a caveat, the purpose being the long run
